title: Column Sorting
details: Every column on the Dashboard and Manage Domains tables can be sorted by clicking its header, and a per-column filter row (hidden behind a small toggle) narrows the tables by domain, status, DMARC and MTA-STS values.

title: Widen alerting beyond MissedReport / TLSRPTFailure
details: Today dotMARC raises alerts for missed DMARC reports and TLS reporting failures. The domain health checklist already checks the DMARC record, DMARC authorization record, TLS reporting record, MTA-STS, SPF, MX and DKIM, but a check going from OK to broken only shows up if someone happens to open that domain.

Proposal: raise an alert when a health check that was previously OK becomes missing or misconfigured, for example an SPF record deleted during a DNS migration or the DMARC authorization record removed. The alert would resolve automatically once the check passes again, respect the existing cooldown, and be delivered through the same channels as other alerts (Teams, generic webhook and HaloPSA tickets).
Why it matters: a DNS change on the client side can silently break reporting or authentication, and today you usually find out days later when reports stop arriving.

title: Allow bulk domain onboarding with CSV or paste-a-list imports
details: Domains are currently added one at a time from Manage domains, which is slow when onboarding a client with dozens of domains or an MSP's whole customer base.

Proposal: import many domains at once from a CSV file or a pasted list (one per line), with optional columns for Group and Tags. Show a preview before committing that flags invalid names and duplicates, then create the domains and start their DNS health checks straight away.
Why it matters: onboarding effort should not grow one domain at a time as your client list grows.

title: Extend DNS Provider push to cover SPF and DKIM record pushes
details: DNS provider push can already create or repair the DMARC, DMARC authorization, TLS reporting and MTA-STS records on Cloudflare, Azure DNS and Google Cloud DNS. SPF and DKIM problems are detected and shown on the domain health checklist, but still have to be fixed by hand.

Proposal: extend the same one-click push to SPF (creating a record, or merging in a missing include without clobbering existing mechanisms and while keeping exactly one SPF record) and to DKIM records supplied by your mail platform, such as selector CNAME records.
Why it matters: SPF and DKIM are among the most common reasons DMARC fails, so they are where a one-click fix helps most.

title: Infer a reason for rejected or quarantined mail when the receiver gives none
details: DMARC aggregate reports can explain why a receiver overrode its policy, but many receivers omit the reason entirely. A rejected or quarantined source with no reason shows as unexplained, which tells an operator nothing they can act on.

When a report gives no reason, dotMARC works out a plain-English explanation from the raw SPF and DKIM results in the report. For example, that no DKIM signature was present, that SPF passed for a different domain than the From: address (so it does not align), or that a check failed outright. It appears on the Sources tab marked as Inferred, so it is never mistaken for a reason the receiver reported, and it is only shown when the receiver gave no reason of its own.
Domain alignment is judged with a same-domain-or-subdomain check rather than a full public suffix lookup, so treat the explanation as a best-effort pointer rather than an authoritative verdict.

title: Audit logging for all changes / configuration alterations and access.
details: dotMARC lets you grant other people (including client contacts) access, change alert and PSA settings, configure DNS provider credentials and push DNS records. There is currently no record of who did what.

Proposal: an audit log that records administrative actions with who, what and when, for example access granted or revoked, role changes, settings changes, domains added or removed, and DNS records pushed. Viewable and filterable behind its own permission, with export.
Why it matters: once other people have access to your dashboard you need to be able to answer who changed something, and many customers and security questionnaires expect it.

title: Add a public API
details: Every integration in dotMARC today is outbound: it calls Cloudflare, Azure DNS, Google Cloud DNS, HaloPSA, Teams and webhooks. Nothing outside can call in.

Proposal: a documented, authenticated REST API covering domains, groups, tags, alerts and report summaries, using API keys whose permissions follow the existing role model (so a key can be read-only or scoped to specific Groups), with an OpenAPI description.
Why it matters: it enables scripted bulk operations, custom client reporting and integrations with tools dotMARC does not support natively, without needing a built-in integration for each one.

title: Add scheduled client report export (PDF and email digest)
details: MSPs typically hand each client a regular summary of their email authentication posture. dotMARC is currently a dashboard you have to open, so there is no report you can send.

Proposal: generate a per-Group or per-domain report (pass rate trends, top failing sources, reject and quarantine reasons, DNS health status) as a PDF, and optionally email it to chosen recipients on a schedule such as monthly.
This is separate from alerting, which already exists.

title: Add a branded client portal view
details: Group-scoped Viewer access already lets a client sign in and see only their own domains, but it still looks like your internal dashboard.

Proposal: per-Group branding (logo, colours and display name) and a simplified client-facing layout that leads with a plain-language summary, so the read-only client view is something you can present as part of your service.

title: Add ConnectWise PSA support
details: dotMARC can open and close HaloPSA tickets from alerts, and resolve an alert when a tech closes the ticket. HaloPSA is the only PSA supported today.

Proposal: the same two-way sync for ConnectWise Manage. Create a ticket when an alert fires, close it when the alert resolves, resolve the alert when the ticket is closed, with per-Group company mapping.
Vote for this if ConnectWise is your PSA.

title: Add Autotask PSA support
details: dotMARC can open and close HaloPSA tickets from alerts, and resolve an alert when a tech closes the ticket. HaloPSA is the only PSA supported today.
Proposal: the same two-way sync for Datto Autotask. Create a ticket when an alert fires, close it when the alert resolves, resolve the alert when the ticket is closed, with per-Group company mapping.
Vote for this if Autotask is your PSA.

title: Add Slack alert delivery
details: Alerts are delivered to Microsoft Teams and/or a generic webhook today.
Proposal: a native Slack delivery option using an incoming webhook URL, formatted like the Teams card with the domain, alert type and message, alongside the existing options.

title: Support multi-tenant mailbox ingestion (admin consent instead of app registrations)
details: Setting up dotMARC currently means registering your own Entra app for mailbox access, granting it Mail.Read, and running Exchange PowerShell to scope an Application Access Policy to the reports mailbox. That is reasonable for a technical team self-hosting, but it is a lot of manual work for everyone else.

Proposal: support a single multi-tenant Entra app, the same pattern dotMARC already uses for Azure DNS push, where an administrator grants consent for their own tenant and picks the reports mailbox, instead of every deployment needing its own app registration and PowerShell scoping. The goal is onboarding in minutes rather than an afternoon.

title: Support multi-tenant dashboard sign-in
details: Dashboard sign-in is configured against a single Entra tenant, which typically means external people such as client contacts have to be invited as guests before they can sign in.
Proposal: support a multi-tenant sign-in app so people can use their own work accounts from other Entra tenants, with access still controlled by dotMARC's own roles and per-email grants.

title: Add forensic (RUF) report support
details: dotMARC deliberately ingests only aggregate (RUA) reports today. Forensic (RUF) reports contain per-message failure samples and can carry personal data, and many receivers do not send them at all, which is why they are currently out of scope.
This idea is here to gauge demand. If you would use forensic reports, vote and comment with what you would need around retention and redaction.

title: Add long-term historical rollups
details: Reports are retained and queryable, but there is no rollup pipeline that summarises older raw data, so long-range trends (12 months and beyond) get heavier to query over time.
Vote if you need year-over-year trend views, and comment on how long you need to keep data.

title: Support sign-in with providers other than Entra ID
details: Dashboard sign-in is Microsoft Entra ID only.
Proposal: generic OpenID Connect support so teams can use Google Workspace, Okta or another identity provider. Vote and comment with which provider you would need.

title: Support reading DMARC reports from IMAP or Google Workspace mailboxes
details: Reports are currently collected from a Microsoft 365 mailbox through Microsoft Graph, which limits dotMARC to Microsoft 365 environments.
Proposal: additional ingestion sources such as IMAP and the Gmail API. Vote and comment with which mailbox type you would need.

title: Add server logs inside the app
details: Diagnosing a failed integration call, such as a HaloPSA request or a DNS push, used to need access to the host's own logs.

dotMARC now keeps its most recent warnings, errors and its own informational messages in memory and shows them under Manage > Server logs, newest first, with level and text filters, auto-refresh and a copy button. Known secrets in URLs and tokens are redacted, access is its own LogsView permission (part of the built-in Admin role), and entries reset when the app restarts. Nothing is captured on demo instances.

title: Recognise more DNS providers and show a domain's nameservers
details: DNS provider detection used to recognise only Cloudflare, Azure DNS and Google Cloud DNS, and everything else showed as not recognised.

It now also recognises Microsoft 365, Amazon Route 53, GoDaddy, Namecheap, DigitalOcean, OVH, Gandi, NS1, DNS Made Easy and Vercel, and the DNS provider row shows the domain's actual configured nameservers on hover, even when the provider is not recognised. One-click DNS push still works only for Cloudflare, Azure DNS and Google Cloud DNS.

title: Show first-seen dates, trends and known senders on the Sources tab
details: The Sources tab now shows when each source was first seen (with a New badge for sources first seen in the last 7 days, judged from the source's whole history rather than just the 30-day window) and a 7-day volume sparkline per source, so a long-running low-grade sender is easy to tell apart from a brand new spike.

Recommendations now name a known email service such as SendGrid, Mailgun or Salesforce when the failing domain matches one, instead of just "a third-party sender", and the suspicious reject activity alert breaks down how much of the volume was SPF-only, DKIM-only, or both.

title: Fix HaloPSA sign-in and priority loading
details: The HaloPSA integration could not authenticate, because dotMARC asked Halo for a scope it does not have, and the priority list failed to load, because Halo returns one row per priority per SLA rather than a plain list.

Both are fixed: priorities are read from Halo's priorityid, de-duplicated across SLAs, and hidden ones are skipped. Errors now quote what Halo actually answered and stay on screen until dismissed, and the webhook URL can be copied with a click.

title: Read DMARC reports that use capitalised or non-standard values
details: Reports from some receivers write values such as Fail (capitalised) or "no policy" where the DMARC schema expects lowercase values, and were rejected, left unread and retried on every poll.

They are now read: capitalised values are normalised and "no policy" is treated as none, while genuinely unknown values are still rejected. Known limitation: a report that uses the sampled_out override reason still cannot be read, because of a bug in the DMARC report library dotMARC uses.

title: Make the Dashboard and domain pages load faster
details: The Dashboard, domain pages and alerting checks loaded every report's full raw XML, and joined related data in a way that multiplied rows and repeated that XML on each of them.
The raw XML is now only read when something actually needs it, and the related data is loaded separately, so these pages should move much less data. What you see is unchanged.

title: Add a HaloPSA integration test that runs the whole ticket lifecycle
details: Until now the only way to know the HaloPSA integration worked was to wait for a real alert, with no way to see where it went wrong.

Alert settings now has a Test the integration button. It creates a clearly marked test ticket from the most recent alert's details, closes it using your closed status, then waits for Halo to call the webhook back, showing each step as it goes. When something fails, the message says what Halo answered or what to check, such as a wrong webhook secret or a status that does not match your closed status. It uses your saved settings, leaves one closed [dotMARC test] ticket in Halo, and does not touch any real alert. A list of recent calls to the webhook shows what Halo has actually sent.

title: Choose which alert types create HaloPSA tickets, globally and per client
details: Every alert opened a HaloPSA ticket, with no way to say that one kind of alert is not worth a ticket, or that one client does not want it.

Alert settings now has a Which alerts create tickets panel with a switch for each alert type. A group (client) can override it from Manage groups: for each alert type it can follow the default, always create tickets, or never create them. A rule only decides whether a ticket is created, so the alert is still recorded and notified, and an existing ticket still closes when its alert resolves. Every alert type creates tickets until someone changes a rule.

title: Assign new HaloPSA tickets to an agent, or leave assignment to Halo
details: Halo will not close a ticket that nobody is assigned to, so tickets dotMARC opened could not be closed again when their alert resolved.

Alert settings now has an Assign new tickets to setting. Pick an agent, or leave it on Do not assign if Halo assigns tickets itself through round robin, a rule or the ticket type default. The PSA docs also list the API agent permissions known to work, and there is a button to clear the cached Halo sign-in after changing them.
